title: GSE_MIND_ARCHITECTURE_SYNTHESIS
universal_lens: Epistemic inversion resolved via deterministic slot-filling frames, numeric containment gates, and mutation-tested constants—aligning GSE reasoning with GSI Bayesian inference through structured symbolic verification. Constrained decoding via XGrammar-2 enables efficient runtime schema enforcement through persistent stack automata and token-level masking, bridging syntactic BPE misalignment with structural state transitions.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over latent belief states; GSE's L3 SAV anchoring ensures numeric invariance, enabling GSI's probabilistic epistemic updates via directional consensus ratios. Bayesian inference in GSI leverages XGrammar-2's deterministic parsing to constrain evidence and mechanism quotes within bounded lengths, enabling probabilistic reasoning over structured game data.
gse_mapping: GSE executes situational reasoning through a four-layer verification pipeline (L1–L4), where each layer enforces logical consistency and semantic integrity, enabling state transitions grounded in empirical telemetry and falsifiable constants. Situational reasoning in GSE utilizes TagDispatch and structural tags to dynamically switch between free-form and schema-constrained generation modes, supporting real-time context-aware narrative synthesis.

primitives.name: Directional Consensus Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Opposing literature claims are evaluated through a directional consensus ratio ($\eta_c$), falling into a deadband ($\eta_c < 0.20$) that neutralizes conflicting evidence rather than overclaiming.
primitives.assumptions: Claims are binary-valued with associated weights; deadband excludes weak consensus.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's directional entropy measure; GSE's L4 NLI entails η_c as a decision boundary for epistemic stability.
layer2.telemetry: Conflicting claim frequency and weight distribution across literature.

primitives.name: Mutation Test 2.0
primitives.verbatim_quote: - The pipeline is guarded by **Mutation Test 2.0**—four orthogonal falsification probes (T1–T4) that fail if any hardcoded constant or templated string remains.
primitives.assumptions: All hardcoded elements must be dynamically derived or provenance-verified.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure of T1–T4 indicates hardcoded dependency or template leakage.

layer2.mapping: GSE's verification kernel maps to GSI's epistemic robustness framework; ensures no hardcoded constants persist in reasoning pipelines.
layer2.telemetry: Mutation probe failure rate per codebase segment.

primitives.name: Numeric Containment Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Ingestion enforces a four-layer verification gate (L1 verbatim provenance, L2 numeric containment, L3 SAV character-offset anchoring with MSVH numeric invariance, L4 NLI mechanism entailment).
primitives.assumptions: All numeric inputs must pass containment checks before processing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Any numeric input violating containment rules triggers rejection.

layer2.mapping: GSE’s L2 gate aligns with GSI’s bounded rationality constraints; ensures numeric values remain within defined domains.
layer2.telemetry: Input value deviation from expected domain boundaries.

primitives.name: Deterministic Slot-Filling Frame
primitives.verbatim_quote: - All prose generation is restricted to a deterministic slot-filling frame with exact character-span provenance.
primitives.assumptions: Prose generation is fully deterministic and traceable to source spans.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Any deviation from slot-filling protocol invalidates output.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI’s generative logic; GSE’s frame ensures reproducible, traceable narrative outputs.
layer2.telemetry: Character span accuracy and slot fulfillment completeness.

primitives.name: Repetition State Compression
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Repetition State Compression**: Essential for enforcing `"maxLength": 240` on `evidence_quote` and `"maxLength": 300` on `mechanism_quote`.
primitives.assumptions: The system assumes that repeated patterns in text can be compressed into compact state representations without loss of decoding fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When character bounds are enforced naively, computational overhead exceeds 500ms; compression reduces this to <5.4ms.

layer2.mapping: Enables hard-length constraints in JSON schema outputs by compressing repetitive internal states during decoding.
layer2.telemetry: Compilation time reduction from >500ms to 5.37ms under XGrammar-2.

primitives.name: CPU–GPU Synchronization Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 1.3 CPU–GPU Synchronization Threshold To prevent the CPU mask preparation loop from stalling GPU forward passes: $$T_{\text{CPU}}(B) = T_{\text{sync}} + B \cdot \left(\frac{t_{\text{mask}}}{N_{\text{cores}}} + t_{\text{xfer}}\right) \le T_{\text{GPU}}(B)$$ - On an H100 with naive Python tensor loops, $B_{\max} = 54$; concurrency above 54 causes GPU starvation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{\\text{CPU}}(B)': 'Time required for CPU processing of B sequences (ms)', 'T_{\\text{sync}}': 'Fixed synchronization delay (ms)', 't_{\\text{mask}}': 'Per-sequence mask computation time (ms)', 'N_{\\text{cores}}': 'Number of CPU cores', 't_{\\text{xfer}}': 'Data transfer time per sequence (ms)', 'T_{\\text{GPU}}(B)': 'Time required for GPU processing of B sequences (ms)'}
primitives.assumptions: GPU performance is saturated when CPU mask preparation exceeds available GPU compute cycles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Concurrency threshold $B_{\max} = 54$ on H100 with Python tensor loops; increases to >256 with optimized C++ APIs.

layer2.mapping: Maps CPU-GPU coordination to a resource allocation problem where $B$ must satisfy timing constraints across both domains.
layer2.telemetry: Maximum concurrent batch size before GPU starvation occurs.

primitives.name: Token-Level Automaton Masking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Token-Level Automaton Masking & Boundary Arithmetic ### 2.1 The BPE Boundary Misalignment Problem Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) partitions text by frequency, not syntax.
primitives.assumptions: BPE encodes text based on token frequency rather than grammatical structure, necessitating explicit masking at token boundaries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misalignment arises when token IDs correspond to multiple syntactic roles (e.g., comma as separator and terminator).

layer2.mapping: Enforces syntactic correctness by restricting valid tokens at each position using automaton-based masks.
layer2.telemetry: Masking efficiency measured via allowed/rejected token counts per archetype.

primitives.name: Structural Tag Dispatch
primitives.verbatim_quote: **TagDispatch & Structural Tags**: High leverage under the **In-Writing Decoupled Protocol**—enables switching from free deliberation (`any_text`) to JSON Schema (`json_schema`) mid-generation without separate API roundtrips.
primitives.assumptions: Free-text generation and schema-constrained output can coexist within a single decoding stream via tag-based protocol switching.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mid-generation transition between open-ended and structured modes requires dynamic protocol reconfiguration.

layer2.mapping: Maps semantic control flow to runtime protocol switching between natural language and structured schema modes.
layer2.telemetry: Latency savings from avoiding API roundtrips during schema transitions.
